name: async_simple (Lazy)
workload: Google Benchmark of C++20 stackless coroutines: a 1000-deep co_await call chain, and collectAll/when_all over 5000 tasks each with a 50-deep chain, run through syncAwait / blockingWait / sync_wait.
claimed_speedup: Lazy chain 59745 ns vs folly Task 195801 ns (about 3.3x faster, derived from page data) and cppcoro task 61308 ns (about 1.03x, derived from page data); collectAll 7880137 ns vs folly 23795927 ns (about 3.0x, derived from page data) and cppcoro when_all 8934768 ns (about 1.13x, derived from page data). Wall-clock Time column.
compiler_and_flags: Clang 13; optimisation flags, standard library, and folly/cppcoro versions not stated
hardware: Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 @ 2.50GHz, 96 logical processors, L1d 32 KiB x48, L2 1024 KiB x48, L3 33792 KiB x2
tradeoffs: Lazy is a lazily started C++20 task type. folly::coro::Task offers more functionality, notably async-stack/context recording on switches for debuggability, which is the cost the doc itself names for the slower folly rows. Stackful Uthread is a separate, non-header-only component. Requires clang >= 10, gcc >= 10.3 or Apple-clang >= 14.
caveats: First-party document whose own closing note says the test is a simple one and does not mean async_simple is better. Flags (-O level), libstdc++/libc++ choice and baseline library versions are missing, so it falls short of tier A. Only task creation, call-chain and fan-out speed are measured, not real I/O or an executor, because the doc says async_simple has no production-grade executor. Doc was last edited 2023-03-24 (file created 2022-02-21) and numbers are from Clang 13. The benchmark source in the repo (benchmarks/Lazy.bench.cpp) contains only the async_simple rows; folly and cppcoro rows exist only in the doc's listing. Against cppcoro the margin is within a few percent on the chain case. std::async is not benchmarked. The repo's other published comparisons (docs/docs.en/QuantitativeAnalysisReportOfCoroutinePerformance.md, Xeon E5-2650 v2, Google Benchmark) compare Lazy only with the project's own stackful Uthread (about 100x faster switching), and docs/docs.en/ImproveNetLibWithAsyncSimple.md shows a coroutine HTTP server at 72363 qps vs a blocking server at 32483 qps (2.2x, Xeon E5-2682 v4, wrk); neither names a listed baseline. Maintainer discussion #309 estimates a coroutine switch costs about 10 ns (estimate, not a measurement).
found_via: seed-record pass; started from https://github.com/alibaba/async_simple (README Performance section), then docs/docs.en/ file listing, which led to Performance.md

name: Fluent Bit
workload: Vector test harness, regex_parsing_performance: each agent receives Apache common-format log lines over TCP, extracts named fields with one regex, and forwards over TCP for 60 seconds, with producer and consumer on separate instances. Also file_to_tcp_performance (tail 10 files, send over TCP, 60 s).
claimed_speedup: Regex parsing: Fluent Bit 3.2.7 20.5 MiB/s vs Fluentd 4.5.2-1 2.6 MiB/s (about 7.9x, derived from page data) and Logstash 8.17.3 4.6 MiB/s (about 4.5x, derived from page data). File to TCP, multi-file (older versions: Fluent Bit 1.1.0, Fluentd 3.3.0-1, Logstash 7.0.1): 35 MiB/s vs 26.1 MiB/s (about 1.3x, derived from page data) and 3.1 MiB/s (about 11x, derived from page data); peak memory there 370.3 MiB vs 890.6 MiB and 763.7 MiB.
stars_or_usage: 8.2k stars; CNCF graduated (Fluentd ecosystem); README claims over 10 million deployments per day
tradeoffs: In the regex test Fluent Bit peaked at 584.5 MiB of memory vs 246.1 MiB for Fluentd (743.8 MiB for Logstash), so the throughput win costs memory there; in the file-to-TCP case it used less memory than both. Written in C with plugins in C, Lua filters and Go outputs (per README).
caveats: Measured by the Vector project (a competing log router) in its public test harness, not by Fluent Bit's authors; results are single runs without variance, and the same tables show Vector beating Fluent Bit on file-to-TCP (76.7 vs 35 MiB/s) and TCP-to-TCP. The harness leaves EC2 instance types to Terraform variables not shown publicly, packages are prebuilt so no compiler or flags exist, hence not tier A. Versions differ per case: the file-to-TCP table is from 2019 releases, the regex table was refreshed in the harness' 2026 update; the Fluentd version label (4.5.2-1) looks like a distro package version, not the Fluentd core version. The harness README warns it is under construction and not fully validated against recent versions. Fluent Bit's own documentation claim of roughly 650 KB idle memory vs about 40 MB for Fluentd (seen only as a search-result paraphrase) could not be opened because docs.fluentbit.io did not resolve; no Fluent Bit-run benchmark was reachable. The harness' TCP-to-HTTP and TCP-to-blackhole case pages were not opened; their Fluent Bit vs Fluentd figures (19.6 vs <1 MiB/s and 64.4 vs 27.7 MiB/s) were seen only in a copy of Vector's README performance table at https://github.com/appsignal/vector, which gives no hardware or versions.
found_via: seed-record pass; started from https://github.com/fluent/fluent-bit (README, no numbers), then WebSearch for Fluent Bit vs Fluentd/Logstash benchmark, which led to https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector-test-harness
